data.title: CTF
data.details:
About

A beginner-friendly online boot2root CTF. Each team gets a vulnerable virtual machine (OVA) to run locally. Your job is to find your way in, escalate privileges to root, and capture the flags along the way. 

Format and Schedule

  • Mode: Online (the VM runs on your own machine)
  • Date: 29 October 2026
  • Start: 6:00 PM IST

Eligibility

  • Open to all college students
  • Inter-college teams: allowed
  • Team size: up to 3 members 
  • Each person can be on only one team

How it works

  • Register on Unstop.
  • The encrypted OVA download link will be shared on 29th so you can download it before the event. The password will be released at 6:00 PM on 29 October.
  • Import the OVA into VirtualBox or VMware, find the target IP, and start hacking.
  • Submit flags on the CTF platform(The URL will also be given on the day of the event). The scoreboard updates live.

System requirements

  • VirtualBox or VMware (latest version)
  • An attacker machine of your choice (Kali Linux, Parrot, or your own setup)

Rules

  • Internet access and public tools are allowed.
  • Do not share flags, hints, or solutions with other teams during the event. Collusion leads to disqualification.
  • Attack only your own local VM. Do not attack the CTF platform, other participants, or any other infrastructure.
  • Do not attempt to brute-force or spam the flag submission page.
  • Do not publish writeups or walkthroughs until the organizers announce the event is over.
  • Flag format: [flag format, e.g. CTF{...}]
  • Ranking: by number of points, ties broken by who reached the score first.
  • Organizers’ decisions are final. Any rule violation can lead to disqualification.
  • If your VM breaks, re-import the original OVA. Contact the organizers if something is wrong with the machine itself.
  • winners must submit a brief write-up explaining their CTF solution. Prizes will be awarded only after verifying that no malpractice occured.

VERSEHACK: WRITERS’ HAVEN

An Online Hackathon by Writers’ Haven

About the Hackathon:

VerseHack: Writers’ Haven is an online hackathon that brings together young innovators, developers, writers, designers, and problem-solvers to create meaningful digital solutions for real-world challenges.

The hackathon encourages participants to combine technology, creativity, critical thinking, and social awareness to develop innovative ideas and turn them into working projects. Participants will explore challenges related to digital culture, information integrity, democracy, accessibility, and equal opportunities.

Whether you are a beginner with a promising idea or an experienced builder, VerseHack is an opportunity to learn, collaborate, innovate, and showcase your creativity.

Tracks:

Participants can develop their projects under any ONE of the following tracks:

  • Digital Creativity & Culture: Use technology to preserve culture, empower creative expression, and make digital experiences more meaningful.
  • Truth in the Digital Age: Develop solutions addressing misinformation, digital literacy, online trust, and responsible information sharing.
  • Democracy, Dialogue & Diplomacy: Build tools that encourage constructive dialogue, civic participation, collaboration, and peaceful problem-solving.
  • Opportunity Without Barriers: Create inclusive digital solutions that improve accessibility and expand opportunities for underserved communities.

Eligibility:

  • Open to participants under 20 years of age.
  • School and college students are welcome to participate.
  • Participants may register individually or form teams of 2–3 members.
  • Inter-college teams are allowed.
  • Team members may belong to different academic specializations or disciplines.
  • Participants from different educational backgrounds are encouraged to collaborate.
  • This is an online hackathon. Participants can work remotely.

Hackathon Format:

VerseHack will be conducted in two rounds.

Round 1: Idea Development and Evaluation | 15 Days 

Date: 15 October 2026 - 30 October 2026

  • Participants identify a problem relevant to their chosen track.
  • Develop an innovative project idea and explain the problem, proposed solution, target users, and expected impact.
  • Submit the required idea proposal through the official submission process.
  • Entries will be evaluated, and selected participants will advance to the next round.

Round 2: Building and Development | 8 Days

data.title: Pixels To Prognosis
data.details:
About the Event

Gliomas are among the most aggressive brain tumours, and outlining them accurately on MRI is central to diagnosis, surgical planning and treatment monitoring. Doing it by hand is slow, and different radiologists often draw the boundaries differently.

Pixels to Prognosis asks you to build an AI system that does this automatically. Using multimodal brain MRI scans, your model has to locate a glioma and separate it into its three subregions: active (enhancing) tumour, necrotic core, and surrounding edema.

The event combines neuroscience, MRI physics and computer vision. You’ll need more than a model with a good leaderboard score. You’ll also need to understand what the scans show, why models fail, and how to make one that holds up on real clinical data.

Who Can Participate

  • Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students from any college and any stream
  • Especially suited to students in Biotechnology & Biomedical Engineering, Computer Science, and AI & Data Science
  • Teams of 1 to 3 members. Cross-disciplinary teams are encouraged.

Competition Structure

Round 1: Online Quiz (Screening)

This is a case-based quiz on:

  • How MRI machines work and the basics of MRI imaging
  • The biology of brain gliomas and how they appear on MRI scans
  • Artificial Intelligence, Deep Learning and Image Processing

The questions reward reasoning over memorisation. The quiz is meant to sharpen your problem-solving for the later rounds.

Round 2: Model Submission Round

Shortlisted teams train a segmentation model on a curated glioma dataset we provide, [derived from the BraTS 2021 challenge]. Each patient has four MRI modalities: T1-weighted, post-contrast T1-weighted (T1ce), T2-weighted and T2-FLAIR.

Your model must segment three regions: Whole Tumour, Tumour Core and Enhancing Tumour. Models are ranked on a hidden patient-level test set.

Rules:

  • Train only on the dataset provided. No external data.
  • All learnable parameters must start from random initialisation. Pretrained weights are not allowed. You may use published architectures such as U-Net variants.
  • The Colab notebook runtime must be 9 hours or less.

Submission requirements:

  • Complete source code (.py / .ipynb)
  • Final trained weights (.pt / .keras)
  • Training logs, including loss and validation curves, config and seed used (.csv)
  • A technical report (.pdf) covering your thought process, pipeline, architecture details and the compute you used

data.title: Hacksprint 3.0
data.details:
HackSprint 3.0 — Build Bold. Ride Beyond.

About the Event

HackSprint 3.0 is a national-level, 36-hour hackathon organized by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Karpagam Academy of Higher Education (KAHE), Coimbatore, in collaboration with the Metaverse Association.

HackSprint 3.0 brings together passionate developers, designers, problem-solvers, and innovators from across India to transform creative ideas into impactful, technology-driven solutions. It provides a platform to experiment with emerging technologies, collaborate with like-minded innovators, and tackle real-world challenges.

  • Mode: Online Preliminary Round + Offline Final Round
  • Final Venue: Karpagam Academy of Higher Education (KAHE), Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu
  • Final Hackathon Duration: 36 hours
  • Application Deadline: 28 December 2026
  • PPT Submission Template: Will be announced soon!

How It Works

Round 1: Online Idea Submission & Screening

The first round will be conducted online. Interested teams must submit a PowerPoint presentation (PPT) outlining their proposed project idea before the application deadline.

The presentation should explain:

  • Problem Statement: What real-world problem are you addressing?
  • Proposed Solution: How will your idea solve the problem?
  • Innovation: What makes your approach unique?
  • Feasibility: How can the solution be implemented?
  • Expected Impact: Who will benefit from your solution?
  • Team Portfolio: Relevant projects, technical skills, and previous work, where available.

The organizing team will evaluate submissions based on innovation, problem relevance, feasibility, technical approach, potential impact, and relevant portfolio experience.

Following the evaluation, selected teams will be shortlisted for the final round.

Important: Submitting an application does not guarantee participation in the final hackathon. Only shortlisted teams will be invited to the offline round.

Round 2: Offline Final Hackathon

Shortlisted teams will participate in the 36-hour offline hackathon at Karpagam Academy of Higher Education, Coimbatore.

Participants will develop their proposed solutions, build prototypes, test their implementations, and present their projects to the judging panel.

Final evaluation will focus on innovation, technical implementation, functionality, feasibility, problem-solving, and overall impact.

Final-round dates will be announced once confirmed.
